SI would have been a better term from the beginning. A lot of people will probably still call it AI, but Optimus is not going to be artificially intelligent, it's going to have super intelligence. It'll take some getting used to lol

Over long periods of time, debts tend to rise faster than incomes, creating the long-term debt cycle.

Even as people become more indebted, lenders freely extend credit because during economic booms, incomes rise, asset values soar, and the stock market thrives. People borrow more to buy financial assets, pushing prices higher and creating a bubble.

So long as incomes keep rising, the debt burden stays manageable. But this cannot continue forever. Over decades, debt burdens slowly accumulate until debt repayments grow faster than incomes. This forces people to cut back on spending, causing incomes to fall and borrowing to dry up—eventually reversing the entire cycle.

The S&P 500 and Nasdaq are trading less than 1% from their all-time highs. Although the major indexes largely avoided the typical August–September correction, significant weakness occurred beneath the surface. Many individual stocks corrected below key moving averages, breadth deteriorated, and equal-weighted indexes weakened while mega-cap strength supported the capitalization-weighted indexes. In effect, the market experienced a stealth correction, stock by stock.

Evidence of that stealth correction can be seen clearly in market breadth. Despite the major indexes trading at or near all-time highs, the percentage of stocks trading above their 50- and 200-day moving averages has fallen to historically low levels. In fact, we have seen some of the lowest participation above these key moving averages ever recorded with the major indexes at or near all-time highs. That is an unusually large divergence between what the headline indexes are showing and what is actually happening beneath the surface.

That could provide an interesting setup entering a historically favorable Q4, particularly during a midterm election year. If breadth improves and previously corrected stocks stabilize and regain their key moving averages, participation could broaden and strengthen the advance. Even without significant broadening, historical seasonality still favors the major indexes moving higher into year-end.

Small-cap stocks, emerging markets, and many cyclical areas have lagged, leaving market

A new Tesla patent application has been published publicly today for a 3D tactile touch sensor for a humanoid robot.

These sensors could allow Optimus to detect touch, pressure, and force across different parts of its hands, improving its ability to grip and manipulate objects.

The 3D tactile sensors can conform to curved geometries and can be used for measuring surface force, touch, and pressure. For example, the 3D tactile sensors described herein can be used in fingertips, palms, end-effectors, or other portions of a robot enabling the robot to sense the world around it. The sensors may be defined using flexible or formable material, such as thermoplastic, and can support resistive or capacitive sensing.

The 3D tactile sensors described herein can be manufactured using a variety of approaches. One example approach involves defining an array of sensing elements in a substrate material using screen printing or substrate etching. Additional approaches involve the use of 3D dispensing (e.g., 3D printing) tech-niques, pad printing techniques, or electroplating tech-niques. The substrate may be formed to a target 3D geometry using thermoforming, injection molding, or compression molding, among any other suitable techniques."

This patent was originally filed in Sept 2025. Tesla may or may not end up using this technology in Optimus: https://ppubs.uspto.gov/api/pdf/downloadPdf/US-202603

By my measurement, the efficiency of intelligence output is doubling roughly every five months. 

This isn't the models getting a bit better... this is the actual amount of intelligence you get out of each unit of energy, doubling, every five months... and the doubling time is shrinking.

Nothing in human history has compounded like this. Not electricity, not the internet. And there's no playbook for it, because every institution we have was built for a world where things changed over decades.

This is what I call The Economic Singularity. Somewhere around 2030 to 2032 the machine economy starts moving faster than the instruments we use to measure it... GDP, earnings, the wage were all built for a world of scarce human labour, all pointed at an economy that no longer runs on it. 

Which means the years between now and then are the window. The whole game is to be positioned on the scarce side of the ledger before the old numbers stop meaning anything, because once the machines are running the machine economy the easy part is over. 

We have maybe five years...

New from the New York Fed: "By February 2026, tariffs had contributed 2.9 pp to goods price inflation, and without them goods prices would have fallen slightly."

About one quarter of every point in higher tariff rates shows up in consumer prices within one year.

• A 10% across-the-board tariff yields a 2.6% rise in consumer goods prices after one year.
• About two thirds of the increase comes from pricier imports, which get passed through quickly.
• Another third comes from U.S. made goods, as producers face higher input costs and less import competition. This takes longer, about 6-12 months, to filter through.
